title: A launched test process never loses its port, and the seek checks finish well inside their bound on CI
description: Two test causes cost JS-167 merge-queue runs this week: a launched process losing its port, and two seek checks with no margin under their 180 s bound on CI. JS-161 lands through the same queue.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/testing.md records queue run 44983050791: the test (TestAProcessWithoutTheWorkerRoleWritesNothingToTheLibraries, shard rest, go test process 2 of 4), which of its 18 processes exited and its log line (bind: address already in use, on the address the harness chose), the cause (the harness closes its listener before the process binds), and what took the port only if shown, otherwise marked unverified

docs/testing.md records queue run 45008394219: the two checks (TestSeveralSeeksInOnePlayOfAFilmWhoseAudioHeadIsLostEachGetTheirSegment, cut at segment 354 of 453; TestASeekPastHalfIntoAFilmReadFromAStoreWithNoPathGetsItsSegment/truehd-6, cut at segment 218 of 229), the cause (a right build's run from the film's start outlasting its 180 s bound), and their times on JS-152's own queue run 44909282472 (197.7 s and 178.9 s against 180 s), saying what each figure times (the whole test and the truehd-6 subtest, both passed)

A check takes, with a real socket, the address the harness chose for a real jellyscale process before that process binds, through the launch the 18-process test uses; before the fix it fails on that process's exit with bind: address already in use, as run 44983050791 did

After the fix the launch survives it: with the port taken once, taken several times in a row, taken for several of 18 processes launched at once, and taken by another process the harness launched (in this go test process or one beside it), each launched process itself answers /healthz on the address its test is handed, never the socket that took the port
What a test reads of a launched process (its log, its exit, what it wrote to its database) is one process's, with nothing of a start that lost its port mixed in

A process that exits for any other reason (a refused config, an unreachable Postgres) is started once and fails its test at once with its log, as today; if the address is taken at every attempt the fix makes, the test fails within a stated number of attempts naming the address, and never hangs

Measured and recorded in docs/testing.md with machine and command, not asserted by a test: 50 runs of the 18-process test under CI's shape (2 CPUs, the rest shard as CI runs it: INTEGRATION_PROCS=4 with the other three processes running), all 18 serving at once in each; in 50 of 50 every process binds and the test passes, and the record says how many launches met a taken port

The port fix is in the test harness and holds for every test that launches a listening process through it, not only the 18-process test. If it needs the app to do anything it does not do for an operator, that is not built and returns as a brief

Measured and recorded in docs/testing.md with machine and command, not asserted by a test: under CI's shape (ffmpeg 6.1, 2 CPUs, the whole of the checks' shard running as CI runs it), in 10 runs of 10, the step the 180 s bound times in each of the two checks (the whole run from the film's start; in the store check, for each of its rows aac-2, truehd-6 and dtshdma-8) takes at most 18 s on a right build; the check logs that time

That margin comes from the run from the start making less film, which a check counts in segments and which fails today (453 and 229 segments): the 180 s bound, go test's 45-minute limit and every other wait of these checks are no longer than today, and the run is not split under several bounds

Each check keeps what it claims: the film whose audio head is lost, one play, and seeks that each start a new job (a short one, one past half the film, one into its last segment); the store with no path, its three audio rows and a seek past half; a burnt image subtitle; every seek's segment compared with a run from the film's start and made by one job begun at that segment. The seek as far in as the dogfood's (1183 s) is kept or its loss is named in the brief below, never dropped silently

Each of the two checks, as shortened, still fails on the build before JS-152 (the product code of b920b19) for the reason it names, shown by its output: the lost-head check at each of its seeks, the seek getting no segment and its job's recorded reason saying ffmpeg made no packet

If less film cannot give the 18 s of the measurement above while a check keeps what it claims and still fails on the build before JS-152, that check stays as it is and the measured times, with what would be lost, return as a brief; no bound is raised and no check, row or seek is removed meanwhile

No retry of a test, no skip, no raised or added timeout; no product code changed to fit a test (nothing outside test files, test scripts, internal/testenv and docs); no other check weakened: the seek matrix (TestASeekGetsItsSegment_*) keeps its film of more than 30 minutes and its seek past half for every row (JS-152 criterion 2); no viewer-visible change
notes: Builds beside JS-161 and never holds it, nor JS-041 or JS-157 (D-050). Merged 730c1ba (#249).
